answers.product.name: phonocompressor
answers.product.description: A phonetic compression engine (Rust, native CLI now, WASM planned) that searches for short exotic-character strings whose TTS reading matches a target phrase.
answers.product.problem: Live-chat TTS messages (e.g. Twitch) have a tiny character budget, and there is no tool that finds the shortest string a specific TTS model will read as a given phrase. Today people hand-craft these messages by trial and error, which is slow, costs synthesis credits, and gives inconsistent results.
answers.product.users: Live-stream chat viewers (e.g. Twitch) who send TTS messages, via the planned web tool; and the developer/researcher running the CLI and test harness to calibrate the engine.
product.goals: Ship the WASM web tool (Phase 3): run the engine fully in-browser
Add more TTS models: calibrate more ElevenLabs models as new ModelProfiles beyond eleven_flash_v2_5
Beat hand-made messages: keep matching or beating hand-crafted reference messages on Whisper intelligibility
answers.guidelines.tone: Concise and direct: plain sentences, state results and limits outright, no marketing language.
guidelines.principles: Measure against real TTS: engine changes are judged by experiments on real ElevenLabs clips (Whisper/wav2vec2), not intuition; results and decisions recorded in docs/PLAN.md
Browser-first, no I/O core: phono-core stays I/O-free and wasm32-buildable; everything shipped must run client-side
Credit-frugal: fit the ElevenLabs free tier; cache every clip, dry-run by default, refuse to overspend an experiment's budget
License-clean distribution: only permissively licensed data ships (deunicode, not GPL unidecode); GPL tooling stays dev-only
answers.tech.languages: Rust (edition 2024, stable via mise) for the engine; Python >=3.13 (uv) for the tools/ harness; TypeScript for the planned web front end around the WASM bundle
answers.tech.database: None: data is a postcard-encoded data/generated/phono.bin built by phono-builder
answers.tech.infrastructure: GitHub Pages (static hosting for the client-side WASM web tool); code distributed on GitHub
answers.workflow.tdd: Moderate: tests encouraged for engine logic (reader rules, scorer, search, data format), not blocking; experiments on real clips remain the measure of quality
answers.workflow.commits: Conventional Commits; no AI attribution lines (no Co-Authored-By or generated-by trailers)
answers.workflow.checkpoints: After each task completion; spending ElevenLabs credits (harness:synth --spend) always needs explicit user go-ahead
answers.styleguides.existing_configs: Use existing configs as source of truth: rustfmt.toml, ruff in tools/pyproject.toml, mise fmt/fmt:check/lint tasks
